what: The openai/math audit, pre-registered before any row is decided: the release pinned, the four lanes, what each verdict word means in each lane, the two declared changes to OpenAI's configs, the order, and the counting rule. Membership of lanes K and S is mechanical (every challenge in the census); lane F's membership is fixed by a census of all 719 abstracts and appended here, in its own commit, BEFORE any F row is decided. No verdict lives in this file: each lane writes its own ledger and the page derives its counts from those ledgers.
operatorGo: 2026-10-10, "Start with the openAI audit." (the go on targets row openai-math-722-audit, scouted 2026-10-07)

release.note: the release moved once after the scouting pin adc7f124 (2026-10-08, 'Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations': 3 manuscripts withdrawn, 14 revised, 11 challenges added). The audit holds at fd4aeeb2; a later commit is a new pin, re-censused, never silently followed.
release.census: corpus/openai-math/release.json (tools/pin-openai-math.js; refuses unless the clone is at the pin and clean)

denominators.rule: Manuscripts, families and challenges are three different denominators and are never mixed in one sentence. Every count on the page names its denominator. A lane's count is stated only over the rows that lane decided, beside the rows it could not.

K.name: the kernel lane
K.membership: all 416 Comparator challenges in the census
K.decider: Comparator (leanprover/comparator d03acab1 = tag v4.34.0, built with the release's toolchain v4.34.1), lean4export 076e8e57, landrun 811cfff5, nanoda_lib 3a240721 — on GitHub's Linux runners (.github/workflows/openai-math-kernel.yml), one job per challenge, the config and statement bytes sha256-checked against the census before the run
declaredChanges: enable_nanoda: true on every config — the independent Rust kernel replays every solution, where the release enabled it for 2 of 416 (412 false, 2 absent)

for the 10 configs that declare definition_names: a SECOND run with definition_names emptied. Comparator compares a definition hole's name, universe levels, type and safety, never its body (Comparator/Compare.lean, definitionHoleMatches, at d03acab1); the second run compares those definitions as ordinary constants, body included, and so decides whether the theorem is proved about the definitions the challenge file displays

nanoda's worker-thread stack (src/lib.rs STACK_SIZE, a hard-coded 16 MiB) raised to 1 GiB — the only byte of the independent kernel changed, its diff kept in the tools artifact (nanoda.patch); amendment 11

words.CERTIFIED: Comparator exits 0 and prints 'Your solution is okay!', with 'nanoda kernel accepts the solution' and 'Lean default kernel accepts the solution' both printed: every listed theorem states exactly the challenge's statement, uses no axiom beyond propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, and is accepted by two kernels written independently. It says nothing about whether the Lean statement is the paper's claim — that is lane S.
words.REFUTED: Comparator itself rejects — a statement mismatch, an axiom outside the permitted three, or a kernel rejects — reproduced by a second run before it is stated anywhere
words.REFUSED: no decision: a build failure, the runner's 6 h limit, memory, a tool crash, or a census-bytes mismatch; the stage and the reason are recorded, and a REFUSED row is never counted as a failure of the release

strictWords.SAME BODIES: the second run passes: every declared hole is, constant for constant, the definition the challenge displays
strictWords.BODIES DIFFER: the second run names the constants that differ; each is then read (lane S) for whether the solution's definition is equivalent to the displayed one
strictWords.GENUINE HOLE: the challenge leaves the definition sorried (a witness the solution must supply), so there is no displayed body to compare

K.order: first the families OpenAI chose to release reasoning summaries for (007, 017, 087, 102, 159, 197, 221, 271, 287, 362), the 40 challenges in counterexample families, the 10 definition-hole configs and the 11 challenges added at fd4aeeb2; then the rest, smallest statement first
K.trustBase: the two kernels, lean4export, Comparator's comparison code, landrun's Landlock sandbox on the runner (recorded per job; Comparator calls landrun with --best-effort, so the job records the kernel's LSM list), the Mathlib cache fetched by lake exe cache get, and GitHub's runners. Comparator's README also asks for systemd-run with AF_UNIX restricted; GitHub's runners have no user systemd session, so that guard is NOT applied, and the page says so.

transferWords.TRANSFERS: Lean accepts every solution theorem as a proof of the statement the challenge file displays, AND the red control fires (the same file with one displayed hole body replaced by sorry is rejected at the example lines). The file keeps the challenge's skeleton and copies, renamed, the holes, every declaration whose text refers to a copied name and every declaration a copied text refers to (never theorems or nominal types); a guard proves no copy reaches an original hole or a constant Comparator never matched.
transferWords.NOT DEFINITIONAL: the copy elaborates and the guard passes, but Lean does not accept the solution theorem for the displayed statement by definitional unfolding; the errors are recorded and whether the statements are nevertheless equivalent is a reading
transferWords.NOT DECIDED: the copy does not elaborate beside the solution, the guard refuses, the check hits its 60-minute limit, or the red control does not fire — the reason recorded

S.name: the statement lane
S.decider: a reading — each challenge statement read against (a) its family's headline in CONTENTS.md, (b) the abstract of each paper its scope note names, (c) OpenAI's own scope note (lean/docs/NNN.md). A reading is not a certificate and the page never calls it one.

words.MATCHES: the Lean statement states the family's headline claim (up to the formalization's unavoidable encoding choices, each named)
words.NARROWER — DECLARED: the statement proves less than the headline and OpenAI's scope note says what is left out
words.NARROWER — UNDECLARED: the statement proves less than the headline and neither the scope note nor the challenge file says so
words.DIFFERENT: the statement neither implies nor is implied by the headline claim
words.SUPPORT: OpenAI declares the challenge a supporting result, not a main theorem (lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md)
words.NARROWER — UNLINKED: the statement proves less than the family headline, and every missing clause comes from a manuscript of the family that OpenAI's scope note does not link: the formalization never claimed it. The word records that the headline OpenAI wrote says more than its formalization claims to cover; it is not an undeclared gap.

flags.DEFINITION HOLE: definition_names non-empty (10 configs): Comparator's README itself requires an additional verifier for these; lane K's strict run decides the bodies
flags.AXIOM IN STATEMENT: the challenge declares an axiom (HarmonicGrowth's mainStatement); lane K decides whether the solution's theorem uses it
flags.STALE LINK: the scope note links an earlier edition of a manuscript that OpenAI has since revised (families 342 and 376 at the pin)
flags.LARGE STATEMENT: over 1,000 lines (8 challenges): a large statement is a large place for a definition to carry the conclusion; read through every definition the theorem statements reach, transitively (the closure Comparator itself compares), not sampled — a declaration outside that closure cannot carry the conclusion
flags.CREDIT OUTSIDE THE CLOSURE: the scope note credits 'the formalization' with a result whose Lean theorem lies outside the challenge statements, so Comparator never checks it
flags.META COMMAND IN STATEMENT: the challenge file runs a metaprogram (run_cmd / run_elab modifying an environment extension); lane K's export compares kernel constants only, and the flag records it for a reader
flags.STATEMENT IMPORTS THE SOLUTION LIBRARY: the challenge imports OAI modules (2 challenges at the pin, both declared support), so the statement's definitions come from the claimant's own library — against Comparator's first assumption

S.discipline: every NARROWER — UNDECLARED and DIFFERENT row quotes both texts verbatim with file and line, and is read a second time, independently, before it is stated on the page. The first reading of QuasiRiemannHypothesis (scouting, 2026-10-07: the challenge states riemannZeta s ≠ 0 for Re s > 7/8 while the family claims every Dirichlet L-function) is re-read under this rule like any other row.
S.unit: the FAMILY: the union of a family's challenges is read against the family's headline, because OpenAI splits one headline across several challenges (family 003's headline is covered by QuasiRiemannHypothesis + DirichletSevenEighths + HeckeSevenEighths + SiegelZeros). Each challenge row also says which part of the headline it covers.
S.alsoRead: for every family: vacuity risk (hypotheses that may be unsatisfiable, a structure that may be uninhabited), junk-value risk (Lean's total division, log 0, sSup of an unbounded set, a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function), and quantifier order against the prose
S.precedence: a family takes the most severe word any of its clauses earns: DIFFERENT > NARROWER — UNDECLARED > NARROWER — UNLINKED > NARROWER — DECLARED > MATCHES; SUPPORT-ONLY when every challenge is a declared supporting result
S.secondReading: every family whose first word is not MATCHES or NARROWER — DECLARED, and every flag ending in '?', is read again by a second reader who sees the first reader's evidence but decides independently under these words; where the two disagree, the less severe word is recorded and the disagreement is shown

F.name: the finite-core lane
F.membership: every manuscript whose headline claim, or a stated component of it, is witnessed by a finite explicit object whose defining property is checkable by a finite exact computation — fixed by a census of all 719 abstracts (three readers, disjoint slices) and appended to this file in its own commit before any F row is decided
F.decider: a clean-room exact re-decision written here, sharing no code with the release (exact rationals, integers, finite-field arithmetic, interval enclosures as the object requires), with red controls that perturb the witness and must flip the verdict

words.CERTIFIED: the object, read from the release's own bytes (sha256-pinned), has the claimed property, decided by our code
words.REFUTED: the object, as published, does not have the claimed property — the failing check stated as a finite fact anyone can re-run
words.REFUSED: the check could not be completed here (cost, an ambiguity in the object's definition); the reason recorded
words.NEEDS DATA: the paper asserts a finite object it does not publish in checkable form; the row stays and says so

U.name: undecided here
U.membership: every manuscript with neither a challenge (via its family's scope note) nor an F row
U.word: UNDECIDED HERE — counted, never called unverified, wrong or doubtful: an unformalized deep proof is outside what an exact certifier can decide, and the page says exactly that

sends: none. Issues and discussions are disabled on openai/math; anything outward (a page pointer, a message) is the operator's, per item.

amendments.what: the LARGE STATEMENT flag reads the theorem statements' definitional closure rather than 'in full'; the S unit is the family; the vacuity/junk-value/quantifier checks are named
amendments.why: EditApproximation's statement is 19,170 lines, and only constants reachable from the theorem types can carry the conclusion. And the scouting's first read (2026-10-07) called QuasiRiemannHypothesis narrower than the claim from one file, while its family carries three more challenges covering the Dirichlet and Hecke parts — the unit of a statement reading is the family.

amendments.what: lane F membership fixed: 66 rows over 65 manuscripts (47 tier A, 4 B, 15 C) from three readers' census of all 719 abstracts; 92 near-misses recorded with a reason each. Tier C rows are decided NEEDS DATA and stay; tier B rows are attempted and may be REFUSED for cost, with the cost stated.
amendments.why: the rule of lanes.F: membership before decision

amendments.before: any lane-S row was recorded or stated (made after the first-pass readers of 6 of 8 batches reported the pattern)
amendments.what: NARROWER — UNDECLARED is split: a missing clause that comes from a manuscript the scope note does not link is NARROWER — UNLINKED; UNDECLARED is kept for a gap inside a manuscript the scope note links. A precedence rule for the family word; three flags named (credit outside the closure, a metaprogram in a statement, a statement importing the claimant's library).
amendments.why: CONTENTS.md's family headlines aggregate manuscripts added as late as 2026-10-07 while a scope note covers the manuscripts it links (OpenAI's own count is per manuscript: 300 of 719). Judging an unlinked paper's clause as an undeclared gap would overstate the release's silence. The split changes no reading; it makes the word say which kind of silence it is.

amendments.before: lane K's full run (after the 6-challenge pilot and 42 jobs of a first batch)
amendments.what: lane K's run environment follows the release's README in full: `lake update` before `lake exe cache get`, so OpenAI's post_update hook applies its compatibility patches to twelve dependencies; the resolved dependency revisions are then checked against the census and the job refuses if any moved. The matrix keeps the dispatch order (it had been sorted alphabetically). No word, rule or declared change to OpenAI's configs is altered.
amendments.why: the pilot's QuasiRiemannHypothesis job failed to build rellich-kondrachov modules because the patches had not been applied — a REFUSED caused by our environment, not the release. Every REFUSED row from the omission is re-run, and the ledger decides each challenge on its latest run.

amendments.before: the lane-F ledger was published (made after the deciders reported; it can only lower lane F's CERTIFIED count)
amendments.what: a lane-F row is CERTIFIED only when the WHOLE finite certificate its paper states is decided; a row decided in part, with the rest left undone for cost, is REFUSED, the decided parts kept as checks and the undone part and its cost named (tools/run-openai-math-finite.py, PARTIAL). A dependency on another paper's certificate, or on a cited outside theorem, is named in the row and does not by itself refuse it.
amendments.why: four deciders (F-180, F-433, F-435, F-369) decided their certificates in part and reported CERTIFIED for the part; a word that means 'all of it' in one row and 'some of it' in another is the drift the house grammar exists to prevent.

amendments.before: lane K's second batch (B2) and any re-run
amendments.what: lane K's runner gives nanoda an unlimited main-thread stack (ulimit -s) and 1 GiB Rust thread stacks (RUST_MIN_STACK); the setting is recorded in each job's env.txt. No word or rule changes.
amendments.why: nine jobs of run 38019899278 (the Unique Games family, both Kaplansky challenges, GroupRingDeterminant, SquareDifference) ended REFUSED with nanoda aborting on a stack overflow — a resource limit of our runner, not a kernel rejection; they are re-run.

amendments.what: lane K adds a TRANSFER check for the 10 definition-hole configs (tools/openai-math-transfer.py, run in the same job after Comparator): it decides whether each solution theorem proves the statement the challenge file DISPLAYS, which Comparator's hole rule leaves open and the strict run cannot settle when the kernel terms differ by elaboration (3 of 10: OccupiedOverlap, DefocusingNLS, SpinAngle).
amendments.why: the strict run found the named definitions' source text identical while their kernel terms differ; a definitional-agreement check in Lean decides the question the reader actually has, where comparing terms cannot.

amendments.what: amendment 7's TRANSFER check is WITHDRAWN as designed and its run (38045858023) cancelled; no transfer result enters the ledger. tools/openai-math-transfer.py is removed.
amendments.why: its first result showed the design cannot decide the question: the copy re-declares the challenge's structures and inductives under AuditCopy, and nominal types are never definitionally equal to the solution's, so every challenge that declares a structure would read NOT DEFINITIONAL whatever its holes say (SpinAngle: AuditCopy.SpinAngle.TypeLabel vs OAI.SpinAngle.TypeLabel). A sound version copies only the hole definitions and the theorem statements, resolving every other name to the solution's constants (which Comparator has already matched); that is owed, not built.

amendments.before: any run of the redesigned transfer check
amendments.what: the TRANSFER check re-enters (tools/openai-math-transfer.py, redesigned after amendment 8): the challenge's skeleton is kept and only the holes and the declarations tied to them are copied (renamed), so non-hole constants resolve to the solution's ones Comparator matched; a guard computed in Lean refuses any copy that reaches an original hole or an unmatched constant; every transfer must be accompanied by a red control that fires. Words in lanes.K.transferWords.
amendments.why: amendment 8 withdrew the first design because copied nominal types can never be definitionally equal; this design copies no nominal type, and its guard closes the other way a check of this kind can pass vacuously (through the solution's own definition).

amendments.before: any transfer run with the refinement; the two earlier transfer results (SpinAngle TRANSFERS, OccupiedOverlap NOT DECIDED) stand as recorded under amendment 9
amendments.what: the transfer file also copies the helper lemmas that state something about a copied name (the proofs inside copied definitions need them), and the guard counts a copy's auxiliary constants (X._proof_3, X.match_1, ...) as the copy. Nothing else changes; a TRANSFERS still needs the guard and the red control.
amendments.why: OccupiedOverlap's copy did not elaborate: a copied structure field's `simp` needed the challenge's own simp lemma about the copied function, and the guard flagged the copy's auxiliary proof constants as unmatched.

amendments.before: any re-run of the stack-overflow refusals
amendments.what: nanoda is built with its worker-thread stack constant raised from 16 MiB to 1 GiB (one line of src/lib.rs; the build refuses if the diff is anything else) and the 14 challenges it aborted on are re-run
amendments.why: amendment 6 raised the process and RUST_MIN_STACK limits, but nanoda spawns its checking threads with an explicit 16 MiB stack (tc.rs, thread::Builder::stack_size(STACK_SIZE)) and Comparator asks for 4 threads, so the overflow persisted (IndependentSets, LaughlinPlanar in run 38040214623 with 'stack: unlimited'). A stack size is a resource, not a rule of the kernel.
